h1: Retatrutide vs semaglutide: a bigger weight number set against four years of outcome data, with no trial comparing them
dek: Retatrutide's phase 2 trial produced the larger figure, 24.2% against semaglutide's 14.9%. Semaglutide has been followed in 17,604 people for about three and a half years and cut cardiovascular events by a fifth. This page sets out what each trial was, what neither shows, and why the second fact outweighs the first.

queries.heading: What about muscle loss?
queries.answer: Neither headline trial reported body composition. A 2026 meta-analysis across weight-loss methods found that about a third of the weight lost on incretin-based therapies as a class was fat-free mass, against roughly 15% for diet and exercise. That is a class figure covering several drugs and it does not separate these two.

queries.heading: Who should not take these drugs?
queries.answer: For semaglutide the label answers this: it is contraindicated in people with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2, and is not for use in pregnancy. For retatrutide there is no label, because there is no approval, so the exclusions are whatever each trial's protocol set. That difference is itself the answer to a lot of questions on this page.

queries.heading: How long can these be taken?
queries.answer: Semaglutide has been given in trials for up to about three and a half years, in the cardiovascular outcome study, and is intended as long-term treatment. Retatrutide's longest published trial ran 48 weeks. Nothing is known about taking it for longer, and its phase 3 programme is what will answer that.

information_gain: The only page on this query to make the comparison about evidence rather than percentages: semaglutide's cardiovascular outcome trial followed 17,604 people for a mean of 39.8 months and reduced death from cardiovascular causes, heart attack and stroke by a fifth, while retatrutide has no outcome data at all and its longest published trial ran 48 weeks in 338 people. The only page to state that the two weight figures come from trials differing by 20 weeks and by a factor of six in size, and that the larger number belongs to the drug with less behind it. The only page to report what the studies naming both compounds actually are, four rodent studies and a set of reviews, and to note that a network meta-analysis's 24,214 participants had been misread as 214 in this record's own drafted data. And the only page to answer the switching question with the fact that nothing has been studied and there is no legal supply.
serp_format_rewarded: A cited comparison. Forbes ranks second and a mouse study fifth, so this query tolerates both mainstream health journalism and primary literature. The gap in all of them is the outcome-data asymmetry.
open_actions: Retatrutide's phase 3 programme is ongoing and unpublished; the page says so editorially with pending_source.
Semaglutide label contraindications are cited editorially; the label is not in this ledger.
